# Sampled touching majorants and the moving-body logarithmic bound

This note proves a fixed-mark lower bound across an actual signed body motion.
It replaces a possibly steep varying concave parameter by a bounded finite-plane
majorant ON THE SAMPLED FIBERS, touching every old positive certificate source.
The majorants converge uniformly through the sampled boundaries. The original
parameters need not do so, and no parameter derivative or moving-row construction
is used.

The proposal is the contributor's sampled-majorant bypass. The finite sampled slope
construction, compactness argument, and signed shell proof are given in full
below. Dependencies are the global contact certificate in
`candidate b2578378c7102b3c`
and, only for the optimizing-parameter application, the interior convergence
theorem in
`candidate b2439018eaa1681d`.
No Gamma payment or differentiability of the optimized buffered value is claimed.

## 1. Actual setting and the old certificate

Let P be finite, in its relative affine span B. Let K_z be positive compact
convex d-dimensional fibers, d>=1, and assume actual compatibility:

    C=conv union_(z in P) ({z} x K_z),     C_z=K_z for z in P.

Write S for the sampled union, dm=sum_z dX|K_z, M=m(S), and let L be positive
continuous concave on C with

    (1/M) integral_S log L dm=0.

Suppose finitely many marks Y_i=(p_i,y_i), with y_i in int K_(p_i), have
positive weights sigma_i summing to one and probability rows rho_i satisfying

    E_(rho_i) w=Y_i,       E_(rho_i) L=L_i:=L(Y_i),
    sum_i (sigma_i/L_i) rho_i=dm/(M L).                     (1)

The only consequence of (1) used for the main proof is the unnormalized
global certificate: for every positive continuous concave V on C,

    sum_i sigma_i log[V(Y_i)/L_i]
         >=(1/M) integral_S log(V/L) dm.                   (2)

For clarity, define d bar_rho_i=(L/L_i)d rho_i. These are probabilities,
sum_i sigma_i bar_rho_i=dm/M, and Jensen gives

    E_(bar_rho_i)(V/L)=E_(rho_i)V/L_i<=V(Y_i)/L_i.

Logarithmic Jensen followed by summation proves (2). Thus the argument below
uses actual full-space row means, never uniform-fiber rows or a continuous
replacement of the discrete base measure.

Let actual compatible K_z(t) converge to K_z in Hausdorff distance, on this
same finite P, and write C_t, S_t, dm_t, M_t for the corresponding objects.
Let U_t be positive continuous concave on C_t, normalized by

    integral_(S_t) log U_t dm_t=0.                        (3)

Assume that U_t converges to L uniformly on every compact subset of the
interior of each OLD sampled fiber, at the same coordinates. These coordinates
belong to K_z(t) for all sufficiently small t. This is the exact topology
provided by the cited optimizing-parameter continuity theorem under its
proper-source certificate hypotheses. The present lemma may also be used
whenever this convergence is established by another argument.

We do not assume L is finite-PL. The construction will in fact exhibit a
finite-plane function equal to L on S. It need not equal the chosen extension
L between sampled bases.

## 2. A finite sampled touching-plane lemma

Fix any actual positive compatible finite family K'_z and positive continuous
concave U on its canonical hull C'. Fix Y=(p,y), y in int K'_p. Choose a
continuous-coordinate supergradient c of U(p,.) at y:

    U(p,X)<=U(Y)+c.(X-y) for every X in K'_p.

Such a finite c exists because y is interior to this full-dimensional fiber.
Define the FINITE collection

    phi_z=max_(X in K'_z) [U(z,X)-c.X].

In particular phi_p=U(Y)-c.y. For every anchored representation
p=sum_z lambda_z z, lambda_z>=0, sum lambda_z=1, we have

    phi_p>=sum_z lambda_z phi_z.                         (4)

Indeed choose maximizers X_z, form X=sum lambda_z X_z in K'_p by actual
compatibility, and apply concavity of U to the actual points (z,X_z).

There is therefore a base slope a in the linear space parallel to B such that

    a.(z-p)>=phi_z-phi_p for every z in P.                (5)

Here is the finite feasibility argument, including boundary bases. If (5)
were infeasible, finite-dimensional separation/Farkas would give numbers
lambda_z>=0 with sum lambda_z(z-p)=0 and
sum lambda_z(phi_z-phi_p)>0. Their positive total permits normalization to an
anchored representation, contradicting (4). A zero total gives the zero
multiplier and cannot give the strict contradiction. This uses only finitely
many sampled inequalities; it does not require an ambient supergradient of U
at Y.

Consequently

    A(z,X)=U(Y)+c.(X-y)+a.(z-p)                          (6)

is an affine majorant of U on EVERY sampled fiber, and A(Y)=U(Y). The plane
is not claimed to majorize U at unsampled real-base points.

We will use a quantitative version of (5). The constraint normals z-p are
fixed. Among its feasible slopes choose one a of smallest Euclidean norm.
There is a constant C_(P,p), depending only on this fixed finite matrix, such
that

    ||a||<=C_(P,p) max_z |phi_z-phi_p|.                  (7)

To see this without any constraint qualification, optimality of the Euclidean
projection gives a in the cone of its active inward constraint normals.
This normal-cone assertion is itself the elementary finite Farkas alternative:
otherwise a separating direction preserves the active inequalities to first
order and decreases ||a||; the finitely many inactive inequalities have slack.
A nonnegative conic representation of a can be reduced to a linearly
independent subcollection I by successively removing a linear dependence
while preserving nonnegative coefficients. For the matrix N_I of these active
rows, a belongs to its row span and N_I a=d_I, where d_z=phi_z-phi_p. Hence

    a=N_I^T (N_I N_I^T)^(-1) d_I.

Only finitely many independent subcollections occur. Their fixed operator
norms prove (7). If a=0 use the empty subcollection. Zero constraint normals
can be discarded. This also treats lower-dimensional B, boundary p, redundant
inequalities, and changing active sets.

## 3. Uniformly bounded planes for the moving parameters

All old marks Y_i remain interior to their current fibers. We first record a
uniform bound on U_t over ALL sampled fibers, including their boundaries.
For each z choose an old interior point g_z and r>0 so that
B(g_z,r) is contained in K_z(t) for all small t. There is a common R bounding
|X-g_z| on all current fibers. Positivity and concavity imply

    sup_(K_z(t)) U_t <= (1+R/r) U_t(z,g_z).             (8)

For X!=g_z use the point g_z-r(X-g_z)/|X-g_z| in the current inner ball and
express g_z as its convex combination with X. Drop the nonnegative value at
the opposite point. The coefficient of X is at least r/(R+r), proving (8).
Interior convergence bounds its right side uniformly. Thus U_t<=B_0 on S_t
for one finite B_0.

Choose any continuous-coordinate supergradient c_(i,t) at Y_i. A common ball
B(y_i,r_i) in the current source fiber and positivity give

    ||c_(i,t)||<=U_t(Y_i)/r_i<=B_0/r_i.                (9)

Apply the sampled touching lemma and use the smallest-norm base slope
a_(i,t). Bounded fiber coordinates, (8), and (9) bound all phi_z and their
differences. Equation (7) therefore bounds every a_(i,t) uniformly. The planes

    A_(i,t)(z,X)=U_t(Y_i)+c_(i,t).(X-y_i)
                             +a_(i,t).(z-p_i)

have uniformly bounded coefficients in the fixed relative ambient space.
Set

    V_t=min_i A_(i,t).                               (10)

This is a globally finite concave piecewise-affine function, with at most one
plane per positive old certificate source. Its exact sampled properties are

    V_t>=U_t on S_t,       V_t(Y_i)=U_t(Y_i) for all i. (11)

The equality holds because its own plane touches, while every other plane
majorizes U_t at that sampled source. Each A_(i,t) is positive on S_t, hence
on C_t by affinity. Thus V_t is positive on C_t for each small t and is a
legitimate concave parameter there before optional normalization. It need not
dominate U_t throughout C_t; this is unnecessary for (3) and (11).

## 4. Uniform convergence of the majorants through sampled boundaries

We claim

    sup_S |V_t-L| -> 0.                               (12)

Take any sequence t->0. Bounded plane coefficients admit a subsequence on
which every A_(i,t) converges to an affine A_i, uniformly on a common bounded
ambient set. Then V_t converges there to V=min_i A_i. For every interior point
w in an old sampled fiber, w belongs to S_t eventually and (11), followed by
interior convergence, gives V(w)>=L(w). By continuity this holds on all S.
Also V(Y_i)=L_i.

Every plane A_i is at least V>=L>0 on S and thus positive on C. Apply (2) to V:

    0=sum_i sigma_i log[V(Y_i)/L_i]
       >=(1/M) integral_S log(V/L) dm>=0.

The nonnegative continuous integrand must vanish on each full-dimensional
sampled fiber, so V=L throughout S, including its boundary. Every convergent
subsequence of plane arrays has this same sampled limit, proving (12).

In particular the old sampled L is the restriction of some finite-plane
function with at most the number of positive certificate sources. This
assertion concerns only S. The original C-extension may be different.

The uniformly bounded plane slopes also show that (12) holds on the moving
fibers in the appropriate comparison sense. Define, separately in each fiber
coordinate space,

    L_ref(z,X)=L(z,projection_(K_z) X).

Then

    sup_(S union S_t) |V_t-L_ref| ->0,                 (13)

where L_ref=L on S. Projection is used solely to define a continuous reference
integrand; it does not transform a body, lattice label, or parameter.
Hausdorff convergence and the uniform Lipschitz constant of V_t prove (13).
In fact V_t has a common positive lower bound on a fixed sufficiently small
neighborhood of each old sampled fiber: combine min_S L>0, (12), and that
Lipschitz constant. Therefore

    sup_(S union S_t) |log V_t-log L_ref| ->0.         (14)

This is the required boundary uniformity. It was proved for V_t, not asserted
for U_t. It uses the old finite-source contact certificate in an essential way.

## 5. Exact finite comparison and signed first-order bound

For small t, V_t is positive also on OLD C, by its sampled positivity. Apply
(2) there and use (11), the old normalization of L, the current normalization
(3), and V_t>=U_t on S_t. This gives the exact finite inequalities

    sum_i sigma_i log[U_t(Y_i)/L_i]
       >= (1/M) integral_S log V_t dm
       >= (1/M) [integral_S log V_t dm
                         -integral_(S_t) log V_t dm_t].        (15)

No normalization of V_t and no comparison at displaced source marks is used.
The second inequality follows because the current integral of log V_t is
nonnegative. It is valid for nested and nonnested motions.

For a concrete shape hypothesis, fix o_z in int K_z. Let the current radial
endpoint corresponding to an old boundary point X be

    o_z+(1-s_(z,t)(X))(X-o_z),
    |s_(z,t)(X)|<=C t,
    s_(z,t)(X)/t -> v_z(X)/H_z(X) surface-a.e.,
    H_z(X)=n_z(X).(X-o_z)>0,                          (16)

with bounded measurable SIGNED v_z. These are the actual signed radial
hypotheses of
`candidate d750a370b2e831ee`.
They allow arbitrary convex boundaries; in d=1 use endpoint counting measure.
Negative v is outward motion. They imply total sampled symmetric difference
O(t) and the oriented radial formula for any continuous reference integrand.

Equation (14) and the O(t) symmetric difference show that replacing log V_t
by log L_ref in the bracket in (15) costs o(t). The oriented radial formula
then gives

    integral_S log V_t dm-integral_(S_t) log V_t dm_t
       =t sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) log L(z,X) v_z(X) dS
                                                              +o(t).

Hence, with the original M,

    liminf_(t down 0) (1/t)
          sum_i sigma_i log[U_t(Y_i)/L_i] >= s(v),
    s(v)=(1/M) sum_z integral_(boundary K_z) log L(z,X) v_z(X)dS.
                                                                  (17)

This is an inequality, not a parameter derivative. The L-values in its
surface integral are old sampled boundary values. All positive and negative
fiber contributions retain their actual signs. There is no collar-contraction
penalty, no pushed-row center displacement, and no unproved changing-parameter
shell expansion.

More generally, the proof requires only sampled symmetric difference O(t)
and the first variation for the fixed continuous integrand log L_ref. The
radial assumptions (16) are a sufficient physical condition, not a necessary
abstract formulation.

## 6. Consequence for optimizing parameters: a fixed-mark scalar lower envelope

Suppose the hypotheses of the cited parameter-continuity theorem hold, and
choose current normalized U_t with actual optimized raw maximum within o(1)
of its infimum; o(t)-accurate choices can be made when comparing derivatives.
That theorem supplies the interior convergence used above.

For the OLD fixed mark Y_i, let B_i(t,s) denote its actual buffered depth in
the current body when its scalar parameter value is s. Its energy, M_t, and
within-fiber covariance are current. All pure-base directions are retained.
At the old proper-gap source B_i(0,L_i)=Q<b_base(p_i). On a common depth
interval around Q, the proper-own-strip argument gives a continuous strictly
increasing scalar inverse s_i(t,q), with

    B_i(t,s_i(t,q))=q,       s_i(0,Q)=L_i.

The old marks remain interior to current fibers; no pushed marks occur.
If q_t=Q_t(U_t), then U_t(Y_i)<=s_i(t,q_t). Therefore, setting

    H_t(q)=sum_i sigma_i log[s_i(t,q)/L_i],

equations (15)--(17) imply

    H_t(q_t)>=t s(v)+o(t).                            (18)

This improves the earlier contraction-collar comparison by retaining the old
marks and the exact signed boundary coefficient. It does not on its own give
a derivative of H_t or q_t. For example, IF a separate all-normal response
analysis proves uniformly for r in bounded intervals

    H_t(Q+t r)=t(A r+B)+o(t),        A>0,

then monotonicity and (18) give

    liminf (q_t-Q)/t >= [s(v)-B]/A.

With M_t=M-tD+o(t), the corresponding normalized lower coefficient is
([s(v)-B]/A+(Q/M)D)/M. If the scalar response has genuine supporting branches,
one must instead use its increasing directional inverse. Neither optimizer
continuity nor this majorant theorem replaces that separate response analysis.

## 7. Exact scope calibrations

### Sampled majorants do not require ambient supergradients

Take P={0,1}, both fibers [-1,1], and C=[0,1]x[-1,1]. The positive concave
function U(z,X)=1+sqrt(z) has no finite ambient affine majorant touching at
Y=(0,0): a proposed finite base slope would have to dominate sqrt(z)/z as
z decreases to zero. Nevertheless the sampled touching construction gives
A(z,X)=1+z, equal to U on BOTH sampled fibers. It lies below U at intermediate
real bases. This is precisely why (5) is a sampled finite LP and why the
theorem never asserts ambient domination. This calibration concerns the
geometric lemma; it is not asserted to carry the full positive certificate (1).

### Downward boundary layers are harmless for the majorants

On K=[0,1], L=1, with the uniform row of mean Y=1/2, put

    U_t(x)=exp[t(1-log 2)] min(1,1/2+x/(2t)),   0<t<1/2.

These normalized positive concave functions converge to L in every interior
core but U_t(0)->1/2. Their touching constant majorant is
V_t=exp[t(1-log 2)], which converges uniformly to one everywhere. This example
illustrates (12)--(14) and does not require the original U_t to lose its
boundary layer.

### A nonzero signed coefficient is sharp

Let K=[-1,1], L(x)=c(1+x/2), where c>0 makes the uniform mean of log L zero.
Set

    y=2/log 3-2,      L(y)=c/log 3,
    d rho(x)=dx/[2 log 3 (1+x/2)].

Then rho is a probability with mean y, E_rho L=L(y), and
(1/L(y))rho=dx/[2L(x)], so (1) holds with one source and sigma=1.
Translate the actual interval to K_t=[-1+t h,1+t h] and take
U_t(x)=c[1+(x-t h)/2], normalized on K_t. It is already an affine sampled
majorant. The inward endpoint speeds are v(-1)=h, v(1)=-h. Consequently

    s(v)=h[log L(-1)-log L(1)]/2=-(h/2)log 3,
    d/dt|_0 log[U_t(y)/L(y)]=-(h/2)log 3.

Thus (17) can be exact at first order with a nonzero signed coefficient.
This checks the sign and the use of the OLD source. It is an analytic
certificate calibration, not a claim that this particular mark is an optimized
buffered deepest point.

The companion verifier checks these exact calibrations and finite sampled LP
identities. It is not a substitute for the compactness, positivity, or signed
shell proof.

## 8. Scope of the new interface

The theorem supplies the fixed-old-mark logarithmic lower bound needed to
compare nearby optimized parameters under actual body changes. It closes the
boundary-layer issue for this ONE-SIDED bound by constructing a different,
uniformly controlled majorant. It does not prove uniform boundary convergence
of U_t, a differentiable optimizer, a derivative of every halfspace minimum,
or equality in (17). No physical row push, equality of volume and surface
couplings, or Gamma payment is inferred.
